title: Scentbird

card.teaser: Rethinking how people discover fragrance in the Scentbird iOS app.

meta: Academic project; mobile app redesign for a fragrance subscription service
Mobile app redesign, user flows, fragrance discovery screens, subscription experience, checkout screens

hero.alt: Interactive Figma prototype of the Scentbird app redesign

text: Scentbird is a fragrance discovery and subscription service that allows users to explore perfumes, receive personalized recommendations, and build a monthly fragrance collection.

Although the concept offers an engaging approach to fragrance discovery, the existing app experience leaves opportunities to make personalization, product exploration, and subscription management more intuitive.
I selected Scentbird for a mobile app redesign because of the potential of its concept and the opportunity to strengthen how users discover and experience fragrance through a digital interface.
I wanted to move away from the conventional beauty-shopping experience, where advertisements and sponsored recommendations compete with what the customer actually needs.

finalDesign: The scent quiz serves as the foundation of the redesigned experience.
I approached the app as a fragrance laboratory, a place where users build their own scent profile through the quiz and can revisit and adjust it at any time.

Eight guided questions explore fragrance preferences through approachable prompts about scent notes, moods, and personal tastes. Rather than relying exclusively on technical fragrance terminology, the questions make preference-building feel more conversational and engaging.

Product listings show how closely each fragrance matches a profile as a compatibility percentage, so the discovery is transparent. Similar fragrances sit inside the product cards instead of unrelated promotions, so discovery grows out of what the user already likes.
The resulting scent profile translates user responses into a signature fragrance family, preferred notes, and ranked recommendations.
Users can review and edit their preferences, allowing them to refine their profile and better understand how their selections influence fragrance matches.
pull: I want to find scents that actually feel like me.

blocks.label: The challenge
blocks.heading: Fragrance is personal, but on a screen, it is invisible.
body: Users rely on descriptions, fragrance notes, and recommendations to imagine how a scent might smell. Without enough context, navigating a large fragrance catalog can feel overwhelming.
My evaluation identified three primary areas of friction:

items.title: Discovery feels like a catalog
items.body: A large fragrance library makes it difficult to narrow down options.

items.title: Recommendations lack context
items.body: Suggested fragrances do not clearly communicate why they match individual preferences.

items.title: Subscription management lacks clarity
items.body: Billing, delivery, and plan management are difficult to navigate.

blocks.foot: The opportunity was to make fragrance discovery more personal while creating a clearer path from initial exploration to subscription.

rows.alt: Three screens of the current Scentbird app.
rows.caption: The current app.
body: I evaluated the existing Scentbird app, conducted competitor research, and analyzed App Store reviews, Google Play reviews, and fragrance-community discussions.
My research focused on three questions:

list: How easily can users discover and evaluate fragrances?
How clearly does the app communicate personalized recommendations?
How easily can users understand and manage their subscription?

blocks.label: Findings
blocks.heading: Three recurring themes emerged

items.title: A lack of transparency behind recommendations

blocks.foot: These findings informed a redesign centered on guided discovery, meaningful personalization, and greater subscription transparency.

blocks.label: Understanding the user
body: I developed a primary user persona, empathy map, and customer journey to better understand the motivations and frustrations behind fragrance shopping.
Maya represents a curious fragrance shopper interested in finding a signature scent and exploring unfamiliar fragrances without feeling overwhelmed by technical terminology or endless options.
Mapping her experience revealed opportunities to support users throughout the discovery process, from initial exploration and evaluation to selecting a fragrance and committing to a subscription.

blocks.label: Design strategy
blocks.heading: The redesign follows four central goals

items.title: Personalize discovery
items.body: Introduce a guided scent quiz that translates individual preferences into a personalized fragrance profile.

items.title: Create a sensory experience
items.body: Make an invisible product more tangible through visualizations, descriptive language, and scent profiling.

items.title: Improve product exploration
items.body: Provide clearer fragrance notes, match scores, and explanations behind recommendations.

items.title: Simplify subscriptions
items.body: Make pricing, delivery schedules, and subscription management easier to understand.

blocks.label: Information architecture & user flow
body: I reorganized the experience around six primary destinations: Discover, Search, Fragrance, My Scents, Profile, and Subscription.
The revised information architecture establishes clearer pathways for browsing collections, filtering fragrances, revisiting saved scents, managing preferences, and accessing account information.
I then mapped the primary user journey, from opening the app and completing the scent quiz to exploring personalized matches, selecting fragrances, building a monthly case, and completing checkout.

blocks.label: Visual identity & interface design
body: I developed a new visual direction using deep purple, electric lime, and soft lavender, supported by editorial typography and geometric scent-inspired graphics.
The visual system creates a distinctive identity for the app while using color, contrast, and recurring graphic motifs to establish consistency across the redesigned experience.
The interface connects onboarding, personalized results, fragrance exploration, and subscription checkout through a cohesive visual language.

The laboratory concept is the foundation for both the visual and the functional direction. I wanted the app to feel like an environment for understanding and finding someone's ideal fragrance, not just a redesigned beauty app.

blocks.label: Outcome
body: The redesigned primary user journey brings fragrance discovery, personalization, and subscription selection into a more connected mobile experience.
By making fragrance preferences easier to express and recommendations easier to understand, the redesign reframes the experience from browsing a catalog to discovering scents that feel personal.

blocks.label: Reflection
body: Sensory experiences can be translated into digital interfaces through symbolism, visual storytelling and thoughtful interaction. It taught me to think beyond a product's usual visual language.

description: Scentbird is a fragrance discovery and subscription service. This mobile app redesign makes personalization, product exploration, and subscription management more intuitive.
